utterances.text: And whilst you were down there at the health centre, did you feel under threat, in peril in any way? Was there any gunfire or was it that you had nowhere to take shelter from possible gunfire from the other side or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No. At that time there was no gunfire, and we were well shielded, because we were behind buildings. The line with soldiers was in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that the soldiers were on the front line and that you were somewhere behind them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes, we were behind the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you behind a building or behind a screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: We were behind a building which was three or four-storey building, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us: During your stay there, was any prisoner killed or wounded in that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I don't know of any of them being killed, but I was wounded. Safet Smajic, that is a soldier, member of Martinovic's troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Where did that happen, and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I don't recall the date, but it was sometime in August, I think early August, 1993. From an unknown direction, a shell fell. It was hot, and we were all out. We were all outside in the street, and this soldier was gravely wounded, seriously, and I was wounded in the stomach. Safet Smajic was wounded in the leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Tell me: Was it in Kalemova, in the base, or was it near the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: It was in Kalemova Street, right in front of the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When that shell fell, when you were wounded, what did you do? Were you taken to hospital? Can you tell us briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I was hit by shrapnel here, because I had my hand here, it didn't pass through. And I had a T-shirt on. So I ran, I dashed into Mr. Martinovic's office and told him that there were wounded, and he immediately dashed out, switched on the engine of a jeep, put us in that car, and took us to Bijele Brijeg, to the war hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did he take you all, the wounded soldier and the two prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Mr. Martinovic took me and Safet, and this soldier had to be taken to the emergency care because he had been wounded in the kidney area, and he almost clinically died on the way to the hospital. I could see doctors extending aid to him, trying to resuscitate him. And we had to wait until that soldier was taken care of. We were lying on beds and waited there for the doctors to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And was this medical aid that was extended to you timely? Were your wounds tended to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, we had to wait a little bit, because there was yet another case, and there were not enough doctors there, so that we had to wait a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Those who were attended to before you, were they more seriously Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. wounded than you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, this guy, this one guy, he was pretty seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: About two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And after that, where did you go, and what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Mr. Martinovic came to collect us, put us in the car, and returned us to the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you then stay at the base or did you go home or back to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: He assigned a soldier to take me home, because I was all covered in blood, so that I could wash myself and change clothes. After that I returned to the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how did you feel? Could you really -- were you up to staying in the base, in view of the status of your health? Did you have to go back to the hospital or did you feel sufficiently well to stay in the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I felt well enough to stay in the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you spend the night in the base? Did you spend that night in the base or were you returned to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: That night I stayed in the base, and the next day I went to the Heliodrom to have my wound dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me: When were you released, and when were you ceased to be a prisoner of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Between the 8th and the 12th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How were you released? Who informed you of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I don't know. I was at the base, and then some people told me that they heard my name called and that I was set free, and then I went to the Heliodrom, to return what was issued to me, and I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you went home. What happened after that with you? Did you start any business? Did you take a rest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: For a time, I took a rest. I didn't go out of the house. Then later on, I started going out. I went to see Mr. Martinovic, asked him to help me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. All this is going very quickly. You said that you returned to Heliodrom, but the reason is unclear. Everything is going too fast and is not precise enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to go back a little and clarify this matter. I apologise that we were too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, my mistake. I didn't warn you often enough to slow down. Now, let us explain the situation when you returned to Heliodrom. The first situation was that after you had been wounded, the following day you went back to the Heliodrom. The reason for that -- what was the reason for your going back to Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: We had a doctor at the Heliodrom. He was also a prisoner. He provided all medical assistance and services to us, and I had to go to have my wound dressed and bandaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The second time when we mentioned your return to the Heliodrom, it referred to the time -- to the date when you were released. Can you briefly repeat how you found out that you were set free? And what was the reason for your return to Heliodrom? Could you please slowly repeat that part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I was at the base the day before I was released. I didn't know I was to be set free on that day. The following day, when men came to work, one of them told me that they were reading a list and that they called my name and that I was set free. On that day I went to Heliodrom, spent another night there, and then the next day, when the officials came, during the working hours, they informed me that I was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: All right. Then you said that you spent a couple of days resting at home and then that you again went to Vinko Martinovic, Stela. What was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, I went to see Vinko Martinovic, to see what was I to do at the time, because I couldn't make up my mind. I told him I had my own garage and that I could work there, I would like to work there, if he could provide protection for me. He advised me to open a workshop and to continue working.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And was that how it happened? Did you continue your work? Were there any problems? Please, slowly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes. I established my own garage and I continued my work. On one occasion an explosive was planted in my garage. It was blown up. But the next day I repaired the damage and resumed my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did Vinko Martinovic come to your garage? Did in any way by his presence provide protection for you. Did he encourage and support you to continue your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: He came on several occasions, or nearly once or twice a week he would come, just that with his presence he would let everyone know that I was under his protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Okay. Just briefly, let us go through another series of questions. While you were in the unit, did you see Vinko Martinovic or any of his soldiers were persecuting or expelling Muslims, or were they in any way treating them in an inappropriate manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I heard of that, but I didn't see it. I did hear of that, but I never believed those stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Why didn't you believe those stories? Did you have different experiences? Did you perhaps have an opportunity that somebody was using or abusing the name of Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may put it another way, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apology. I think your objection is in place. It was not my intention to lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You said you didn't believe those stories. Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Since, as a Muslim, I was in Stela's base, I, just like many other men, never experienced any -- never had any unpleasant experience, and I couldn't believe that that was possible to happen to someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Have you ever personally seen a crime committed and that somebody was impersonating Stela or any of his soldiers? Have you personally witnessed such a situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion I did. Under the window of my flat, sometime after midnight, somebody was breaking into a car, and I heard voices saying, "Hurry up, Stela." Knowing Stela, I pushed up the blinds, and I wanted to tell him that that was my car, in fact, that he should leave it alone. But I didn't see Stela. One of the two men pointed the rifle at me and ordered me to close the blinds, which I -- and I complied.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So when you heard the name "Stela" mentioned, did you recognise Stela among the two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Have you ever heard or seen directly and personally the police asking or discussing with Stela about various crimes that were being committed in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Once we were working on a vehicle. We stayed late in the night, maybe until 9.00 p.m. We brought the vehicle back to the base. Stela invited us to a cafe nearby, next to the base. We were sitting there and a quite a few drinks, and it lasted until 1.00 or 2.00 in the morning. On that night, the civilian police came and they told Stela that they received three reports from citizens about some kind of theft, that his name was mentioned, whereas he spent the whole time with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions, Your Honours. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think we'll make a break here and we'll resume until 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Perhaps we should go into private session in the beginning of cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you have any specific task for the 9th of May, as a soldier of Armija, member of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you explained to the Trial Chamber that after the 9th of May, it was impossible to use your workshop; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I would ask you to -- just to give a little more details about what happened on the 9th of May. In the area, at least, where you were living, and indicated on the map. Did you see any mass movement of the population towards the Velez Stadium on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I went regularly to do my job as a mechanic. The street that I was walking down towards my work is not in any way connected to the way to the stadium, and I couldn't see or notice any movements or any major crowds in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I would like to clarify my question. I meant the 9th of May, 10th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, I returned, but I didn't have access to my workshop. At one corner was the HVO army, troops. One of them, aka Pinda, recognised me and warned me not to proceed further and to go back home and to stay at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you see any of your neighbours arrested on the 9th of May, or did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I heard about it only in the evening of the 9th of May, but there were none of my neighbours among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were any of your next-of-kin arrested on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes. My brother was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was he released in May or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know who arrested him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When was he released, and where was he kept before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: He was detained at Heliodrom and was released on the 19th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you meet him in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: When I was released, after that I went to visit him, two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you mean you went to visit him to Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So, Witness, is it your testimony that nothing special was happening in Mostar as from the 9th of May to the 30th of June, 1993? Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, I don't exactly claim that nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you, why, at some point you decided to turn to Vinko Martinovic for some assistance. What did you fear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, I was afraid precisely because my brother was detained, and I feared that the same might happen to me, and that is why I sought assistance and help.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what kind of assistance did you expect from Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, mainly to protect me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was he a very important person, a person with consequences [As interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, not of great influence, but he had authority that he acquired back from the time of HOS units, and I had a feeling that he could help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did he occupy any important position in Mostar at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was he a civilian, just a layman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: When I met him on avenija, as I said in my statement, he was in a car. He was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: My question is wider. Your contacts with Vinko Martinovic were not limited to the day in May or June. You had some communication with him later. What was your perception? If he occupied any position or position in some civil administration that could be very important and gave him vast powers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, he wore a uniform, just like everybody else, but I don't know if he occupied any position, that he had some rank or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how do you think he was able to protect you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, probably by his authority from HOS. People had respect for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, but it's quite clear that HOS did not exist at that time. It ceased to exist somewhere in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What kind of authority do you mean, then, that Stela might have at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I'm speaking about how people in the army respected him, people from his own national group. He was a well-known figure in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But why do you think that you should have expected some misdoings from military persons, from military people who respected Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, I didn't expect that exactly from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: From whom did you expect any misdoings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I wasn't afraid of Croats born in Mostar, but from Bosnia there was an influx of people from Konjic, Jablanica, Sarajevo, and that is what I feared the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you mean Croats, influx of Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And again I would like to return you to your brother. Was your brother a military man at the moment when he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was he of military age, I mean from 18 to 60?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know now who arrested him? I don't mean the personality who executed the arrest; I mean the organ, organisation, body who arrested him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You don't ask him? You never asked him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: He didn't know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Perhaps he was arrested by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. Argumentative. These questions are becoming argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I think, you know, the witness answered the question. He doesn't know. He didn't know either. I think there's no need, you know, to ask more questions in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. You're right. Since the witness is so indifferent to his brother. But I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that this comments, like the most recent one, are inadmissible in a courtroom. I think that in a way this is an inadmissible treatment of the witness, and even the previous question, when my learned colleague asked whether there were Serbs, I think that was a certain provocation towards the witness. I really want our witnesses to receive at least the same treatment as the witnesses, and we know that the Court takes due care of protection of witnesses who are also victims, and we -- I kindly ask that they be treated in an appropriate manner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, be careful with the words you are using. Do not use any provocative words towards any witness. I understand it's difficult in conducting a cross-examination, but just have some patience and politeness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I never lose my countenance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, and who was running Heliodrom? Who was keeping you in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I cannot answer that. I was simply arrested. There were guards around us. I can't tell you had who kept me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: To which military organisation, military police, did those guards belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Probably the command of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Who was in command of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Okay, Witness. You were talking about two conflicting forces in Mostar, and even about skirmishes between them. It was Armija and HVO; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You were not arrested by the Armija soldiers; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. I didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I didn't hear him either.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on to the 30th of June. So you explained to the Trial Chamber that very important events occurred in Mostar on the 30th of June, 1993. Do you remember at what time those events started on the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: These events happened on the left bank. I was living on the right bank. I don't know exactly when they started. I -- it was just announced on the radio that the Northern Camp had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was it announced in the morning, in the afternoon, or at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Exactly at 11.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So, and you explained to the Trial Chamber that you had some speech by Arif Pasalic; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was it the only speech by Arif Pasalic that you had on the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And if I follow well your testimony, you just claimed that Pasalic called Muslims who lived on the western part of Mostar just to put up resistance to ABiH; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: To HVO, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Oh, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Today you told to the Trial Chamber that you heard Mr. Pasalic, and in his speech he called the Muslims who lived on the west part of Mostar to put up resistance to the HVO; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did he call Muslims to attack the HVO troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you now. Well, I will repeat precisely what he had said. "Muslims on the right bank, take rocks and stones into your hands and confront the Ustasha."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Rocks and stones; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: That's right. This is my precise response.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I appreciate your response. Witness, again, according to your testimony, that on some sixth or seventh day after your arrival to Heliodrom, you were taken to Vinko Martinovic's place to work; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I received a message from my wife, who asked that I go to Vinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you were taken to Vinko Skrobo's place; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And who took you there in that black -- blue truck? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: All I know is that the driver's name was Dinko. I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was it the same Dinko who took you to that place on other occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe now we should go into a private session for some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, but can I ask Your Honours and my learned friend: My direct examination lasted 45 minutes, and could this be done within the time? It would be good to finish this witness today, because the Victims and Witnesses Unit has done all to have this group of witnesses on their way tomorrow, so I would appreciate it if the examination of this witness could be concluded today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like to do it, but not to the detriment of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, do you know any of Stela's soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Please, to the best of your recollection, please, could you give us some names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I know brothers Colak, I know Vlaho, I know the Peric brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you know Ernest Takac, Dubravko --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of position they occupied, I mean the last two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I think they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, you just explained to the Trial Chamber that at some point soldiers paid you by buying you cigarettes, food, and something else, some minor things; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: They didn't give us other things, but when it was time for a salary, they gave me money; they didn't give me any things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Who gave you a salary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Not to me. I mean when the troops received their salaries, then for the services that I rendered them, they would remunerate me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Or better to say, your clients?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, perhaps later on when I started working in my own workshop, it is then that they became my clients.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So it was not Stela who paid you; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Not right. I could never pay back to Vinko Martinovic in any way for what he did for me. He's always paid me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, if Vinko Martinovic was the only "Stela" around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And is it correct, Witness, that on one occasion you heard some voices, something about Stela, when some people, soldiers, tried to steal some vehicle? Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Why can we assume that it was his soldiers who were stealing things? "Not" should be in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, I guess they would have recognised me had I drawn up the blinds, but I do not think they would have aimed their rifles at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So they didn't recognise you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What kind of vehicles did you repair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Well, usually small passenger cars, those that the troops used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you mean --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you mean the vehicles that were used by soldiers, by troops? Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did they have military plates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I am coming up to the end. My final -- pre-final question, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness, did you sign any declaration while you were kept in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you hear about any declaration that was circulated among Muslim prisoners in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very disciplined, so I completed my cross-examination 45 minutes sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination? Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one question. Thank you. I'd like to thank my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, do you know whether there is somebody else who is called Vinko Martinovic, Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No, not Stela, but another Vinko Martinovic,

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Like Vinko Martinovic present here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MI
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of such person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much for coming to give your evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. All of us wish you a pleasant journey back home and a good business in the future.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. Only the map, D2/33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. I have no documents to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So this document is admitted into the evidence, under seal. Well, Mr. Par, we have received a list for the witnesses of the next week, and I'm a little bit concerned that we will have five witnesses on the list. According to the speed we are now, probably we could finish that list by Wednesday. Are you considering to have one or two more witnesses for next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we provided a list of five witnesses because we thought that would fit into the schedule that we were given. We thought that that would be a sensible number of witnesses, because we do not want to have a witness who will be here, wait, and then come back only after the summer recess. The next group of witnesses are witnesses who will not be repetitive, meaning the witnesses who were here. We are beginning with a new group of witnesses, and these are soldiers, members of the Vinko Skrobo unit, and I believe that their examination will take longer, at least that the cross-examination will take longer. And we thought -- we think, therefore, that five witnesses is quite a reasonable number. If we finish a day earlier, I think it is better than to have somebody left over. And another matter: I do not think that it will be technically possible for us to get another witness here, and we somehow thought that if would be 15 witnesses. We notified everybody else. It is time of -- it is the holiday season and I'm not even sure whether we would be able to get anyone to come here now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That sounds reasonable. Are there any protective measures you are asking for those witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For those witnesses, we are asking for the same protective measures as before, except that it is quite possible, when one of those soldiers come, perhaps they will not need all the protective measures that we applied for. So perhaps they will not need voice distortion or even pseudonyms. Right now we thought it would be better to be cautious and we applied for all the protective measures, so perhaps we shall renounce some of the protective measures. We shall not be asking for more protective measures for these witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And I believe that the voice distortion will take, you know, much effort to do it. And frankly speaking, I'm not quite convinced by the voice distortion. So you may reconsider, you know, that, you know, request during the weekend. But anyway, we'll have all the protective measures in place just in case. So I understand -- Mr. Scott, I have something to address to this Bench, but I see there's only ten minutes left. If you could finish your statement or whatever you want to say in ten minutes, you may go on, but if not, tomorrow we'll have the whole day for those procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I can try. Perhaps the most important thing, as I mentioned the other day, if I can alert the Chamber to the issue before we go into recess and we now have -- we will have next week for the Chamber to consider what steps, if any, the Chamber would want to take in order to provide for the most efficient handling of the case after the recess. I think -- so I think I can cover it substantially, Mr. President. To assist the Chamber, I have prepared just a one-page handout that maybe will assist in covering it as efficiently as possible. If that could be provided, please, to Defence counsel and to Your Honours. It's just simply a list of names, and I think it's best, Mr. President, to do this most efficiently and quickly if we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 7.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 29th day of July 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
